config.detail: No HF config.json: the repo ships ONNX files only. Geometry from train.py (WhisperEncoder from whisper-tiny with config.max_source_positions = 400; pool_attention Linear(384,256)-Tanh-Linear(256,1); classifier Linear(384,256)-LayerNorm(256)-GELU-Dropout-Linear(256,64)-GELU-Linear(64,1); sigmoid), confirmed against the ONNX graph and initializer shapes by scripts/convert-smart_turn.py (check_graph / check_geometry).

preprocessor.detail: truncate_audio_to_last_n_seconds(audio, 8): keep the last 128000 samples or left-pad with zeros to 128000; WhisperFeatureExtractor(chunk_length=8)(..., padding='max_length', max_length=128000, truncation=True, do_normalize=True): zero mean / unit variance over the whole 128000-sample window (padding included, eps 1e-7, float32), then Whisper log-mel (reflect pad 200, periodic Hann 400, hop 160, |X|^2, slaney 80-bin filterbank, log10 floor 1e-10, drop last frame, clamp to max-8, (x+4)/4) -> [80, 800].

safetensors_metadata.detail: No safetensors. The fp32 ONNX (opset 18, exported by pytorch 2.9.0+cu128) holds 8,000,386 float32 weights: 53 named inner.* initializers plus 26 anonymous, transposed MatMul weights (val_17 ...), named by graph walk in scripts/lib/smart_turn_onnx.py.

reference_modeling_code.path: onnxruntime on smart-turn-v3.2-gpu.onnx, run as smart-turn inference.py predict_endpoint
reference_modeling_code.detail: Upstream's own inference path (inference.py; Pipecat LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3 runs the same graph with a vendored numpy copy of the feature extractor). Instrumented twin: train.py's SmartTurnV3Model rebuilt in transformers 4.48.2 with the ONNX weights mapped in; matches onnxruntime to <= 5.4e-6 in p on the golden clips and <= 5.4e-7 on random inputs.

dtype.evidence: Every initializer of smart-turn-v3.2-gpu.onnx is float32 (the fp32 export; README: 'GPU version uses fp32 weights'). smart-turn-v3.2-cpu.onnx is upstream's static int8 QDQ quantization of the same model and is not a conversion source.

upstream_benchmarks.notes: fp32 ONNX (smart-turn-v3.2-gpu.onnx), 31,527 clips, 23 languages, decision p > 0.5. Measured by scripts/turn/run_reference_smart_turn_onnx.py (onnxruntime 1.23.2, arm64): 93.71%, FPR 3.51%, FNR 2.78% of 31,527, identical to the published report. TURN role: binary end-of-turn accuracy, not WER.

Upstream's int8 ONNX (smart-turn-v3.2-cpu.onnx), same 31,527 clips; the bar our quantized GGUFs are compared to. Measured: 92.62% (FPR 4.76%, FNR 2.63%); published 92.63% (FPR 4.73%, FNR 2.64%): int8 kernels differ by host.

reference_rationale: Upstream publishes only ONNX files and runs them with onnxruntime (smart-turn inference.py, Pipecat LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3); no PyTorch checkpoint exists. The canonical reference is therefore onnxruntime 1.23.2 on the fp32 ONNX at the pinned HF revision, CPU, 1 thread, with transformers 4.48.2's WhisperFeatureExtractor on its numpy path (the path inference.py's requirements and Pipecat's vendored copy run). Intermediates come from the same graph with the dump points exposed as outputs; a PyTorch twin (train.py SmartTurnV3Model with the mapped weights) is the instrumented cross-check.
known_risks: Role is TURN (new role, include/transcribe/turn.h): acceptance is head.prob parity and decision parity (p > 0.5) with onnxruntime on the golden clips and on pipecat-ai/smart-turn-data-v3.2-test, plus test-set accuracy vs the measured reference; not WER, and LibriSpeech does not apply.

ONNX-only source: 26 Linear weights are anonymous MatMul initializers stored transposed ([in, out]); they are named by graph walk (the bias Add consuming each MatMul, or for k_proj the layer's self_attn_layer_norm), and the mapping is validated by reloading them into train.py's SmartTurnV3Model.
Fixed 8 s window: input longer than 128000 samples keeps its LAST 8 s; shorter input is LEFT-padded with zeros. Audio before the last 8 s has no effect.

Waveform normalisation runs over the whole padded window (padding included), so the amount of padding changes the statistics; the C++ must normalise the 128000-sample window, not the clip. All-zero input has variance 0 and relies on eps 1e-7 (features become a constant -1.5).

Front end: transformers picks a float32 torch STFT when torch is importable and a float64 numpy STFT otherwise; the reference pins the numpy path (inference.py's requirements and Pipecat's production copy). The mel filterbank is computed by transformers (mel_filter_bank, slaney), not whisper-tiny's preprocessor_config table.

Whisper massive activations: from encoder block 2, channel 375 (then 16, 128, 247) reaches |x| 80-153 at a few positions, so fp32 reduction order moves enc.block.2/3.out by up to 2e-2 between two correct implementations (PyTorch twin vs onnxruntime); p moves by <= 5.4e-6. Stage 4 will likely widen those tolerances.

Positional table has 400 rows and is close to but not exactly transformers' sinusoids(400, 384) (max 3.1e-5 off, an export-time float difference); the GGUF stores the exported table and the C++ must load it, not recompute it.
Attention: the k projection has no bias (Whisper); the export splits the 1/sqrt(64) scale as 64**-0.25 on q and on k (torch SDPA decomposition).
Decision rule: upstream uses p > 0.5; the draft TURN API uses p >= threshold (docs/turn.md O2). Silence scores p = 0.4615, close to the cut-off.
No streaming: the model scores one clip per call; transcribe_turn_stream_* is NOT_IMPLEMENTED for this family.

Upstream's int8 ONNX (static QDQ) is a different artifact from our GGUF quants; its accuracy (92.63% published, 92.62% measured) is the comparison point for Stage 5. It disagrees with fp32 on 3.9% of test-set decisions (silence: fp32 0.46, int8 0.99).
Quant policy: head.cls.1.weight is a LayerNorm scale whose name the norm rules in reference_dtype_for / policy.cpp do not match; Stage 5 must keep it (and all 1-D head tensors) F32.
